reason: The text is the Book of Jonah and does not contain any instance of the Hebrew people complaining about their leaders. Instead, it narrates: (1) God's command to the prophet Jonah to preach to Nineveh; (2) Jonah's disobedience and flight; (3) a storm at sea involving gentile sailors from a ship bound for Tarshish; (4) Jonah being cast into the sea and swallowed by a great fish; (5) Jonah's prayer and deliverance; (6) the repentance of the people and king of Nineveh (an Assyrian city, not an Israelite population); and (7) God's dialogue with Jonah about divine mercy. The only discontent expressed is Jonah's personal anger at God's mercy toward Nineveh, not the Hebrew people's complaints about their leaders.
